text: This is OpenRampKit. Unified deposits and withdrawals for any app. The RainbowKit for onramps and deposits.
It is open-source deposit infrastructure for crypto apps. It solves the onboarding chasm: getting billions of users onchain. This playground runs the real server in your browser, with mock providers.
Our user is in Vietnam. Under Use Cash, they see local methods. They pick VietQR and enter five hundred thousand dong.
The pathway planner asks each provider for a quote. Three providers answer. The best price comes first.
They scan the VietQR code with any banking app. In test mode, we simulate the payment.
Deposit complete. Your page gets widget events. Your backend gets a signed webhook, and the signature checks out.
Now a user in the United States. Card, Apple Pay and Google Pay are there. They pick card and compare quotes.
They type the test card number, the expiry and the CVC right in the widget. Then they pay with the test card.
Some users keep their funds on an exchange. From an exchange shows a deposit address, with the network and the token. They send USDC from their exchange account.
You choose which payment sources to offer. Turn off card, and it is gone. Then match your brand with theme, corners and font.
The same kit handles the way out. The user withdraws USDC to a bank account. They get a payout quote in local currency.
They enter their bank details. Then they approve one transaction in their wallet, and the provider pays out in dong.
For developers, it is a few lines. Create a session on your server. Open the widget on your page.
Ten provider adapters, from card onramps to local rails. Self-hosted, next to your own backend.
Settlement is onchain. OpenRampSettlement is live on Arbitrum Sepolia and Robinhood Chain testnet. One transaction emits a Settled event that your app can verify.
AI agents can use it too. Through MCP, an agent creates a pay link, and a person pays. OpenRampKit. MIT licensed. Get your users onchain.
